newsitem.title: USA: Lawsuit seeks to block TVA's Trico power contract.
newsitem.headline: Lawsuit seeks to block TVA's Trico power contract.

text.p: Four members of the United Steelworkers of America are seeking to enjoin Tennessee Valley Authority from selling power to Trico Steel, the union said Monday.

In a lawsuit filed in U.S. District Court in Alabama, the four Alabama residents charge TVA acted unlawfully in agreeing to provide Trico Steel "the largest package of economic incentives' offered in TVA's history," the steelworkers said.
Plaintiffs in the action are W.W. Winkles, Clyde Dial Jr., Danny Ray, and E.V. Tucker, all of them residential customers of TVA generated power. Ray also is a TVA bondholder.
TVA officials did not respond immediately to requests for comments on the suit.
The plaintiffs state that TVA is charging Trico an estimated $0.01 per kilowatt hour, the union said.
"Residential customers of TVA in the same area pay up to $0.05 and $0.06 per kilowatt hour," it added.
Trico is a venture of LTV Corp, British Steel and Sumitomo Metal Industries Ltd.
The union said the four plaintiffs allege that following LTV Steel's December l994 announcement of its Trico venture, the TVA's board named David N. Smith chief financial officer.
Prior to his appointment by TVA, Smith had served as LTV's Vice President-Finance, the suit notes.

The complaint further states that, within about six months of Smith's appointment as CFO of TVA, LTV announced its decision to locate Trico in Decatur, Ala. -- part of the TVA service area -- and TVA announced it was granting to Trico what plaintiffs describe as "the largest package of economic incentives' offered in TVA's history."
The discounted TVA power contract, the lawsuit alleges, grants Trico what plaintiffs estimate to be an annual benefit of $28.7 million.
